pros: Handles disconnected graphs naturally (1/∞ = 0, not undefined)
More robust to distant outliers than closeness centrality
Simple to compute: BFS + sum of reciprocals
No special handling needed for disconnected components
Monotonically increases with added edges (always beneficial)
Normalized version ranges from 0 to 1 for all graphs
Less sensitive to small graph changes than betweenness
Can compare nodes across different components
Identifies nodes that can efficiently reach all others
Works with both directed and undirected graphs
cons: Same O(V·(V+E)) time as closeness — impractical for very large graphs
Memory overhead for storing distances during BFS
May not distinguish nodes in well-connected dense graphs
Reciprocal transformation compresses large distance differences
Less established in literature than closeness or betweenness
Weighted version requires Dijkstra, increasing time by log V factor
Not suitable for real-time dynamic graph analysis
Approximation algorithms less developed than for betweenness
Score interpretation varies with graph size and density
O(V²) for sparse graphs still expensive for n > 10⁵
